Subject: SLA hit on 2027-06-12 — probe coverage attached / request exclusion

Hi Priyom,

We completed an audit of our downstream metrics and noticed a sustained partial degradation on 2027-06-12 between 21:06 UTC and 21:17 UTC that pushed availability below our contract SLO for that minute granularity. We see 11 minutes of degraded responses impacting our API endpoints (attached: customer-probes-20270612.zip).

Redwood's incident page listed a scheduled maintenance window that overlaps parts of this period. DataMap requests that this overlap be excluded from the uptime calculation per section 4.2 of our SLA, or alternatively confirm why the event is considered third-party and not Redwood-maintenance.

Please advise what logs/traces you need from us. We need confirmation of whether we will receive a credit and the calculation used — the account team indicated this might be escalated.

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2027 11:05:12 -07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: DataMap probe/maintenance overlap — suggested stance

Team — forwarding DataMap's probes. Summary: 11 minutes of partial degradation reported by the customer on 2027-06-12 (21:06–21:17 UTC). Our maintenance calendar shows a low-risk config rollout window in the same region from 21:00–21:10 UTC that was announced three days prior (change ID CH-1927). The overlap is 4 minutes (21:06–21:10). Customer claims the full 11 minutes should be excluded.

Quick analysis so far:
- Our per-POP telemetry shows elevated p95 latency and increased 502 responses between 21:06–21:17 concentrated on POPs x-us-west-2-a and x-us-east-1-b.
- The scheduled config change touched TLS reconfiguration on the edge layer and completed at 21:10 with normal health checks.
- Customer probe traces indicate path asymmetry; several of their probes traversed AS64532 (third-party transit) which experienced short flaps at 21:11–21:16 per their pcap.

Options:
A) Treat the 21:00–21:10 window as maintenance-excluded per SLA (4 minutes excluded), and grant a partial credit for the remaining 7 minutes if we determine residual impact was on Redwood's edge (customer visible errors served by our servers).
B) If we classify the primary cause as third-party transit (AS64532) for the residual minutes, we deny credit for those minutes.

My recommendation is to offer a blended outcome: exclude the announced maintenance portion and offer a one-time goodwill credit for the remaining minutes (calculated pro rata) while committing to a joint post-mortem. This reduces friction and preserves the relationship.

Marissa/Ben — thoughts, and do you concur with pursuing option A + goodwill? Also, Ben — can you produce a short packet-level mapping and the redwood-traces file by EOD?

Thanks,
Priyom

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2027 13:18:45 -07:00
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: DataMap probe/maintenance overlap — suggested stance

On Tue, Jun 30, 2027 at 11:05 AM Priyom Das wrote:
> My recommendation is to offer a blended outcome: exclude the announced maintenance portion and offer a one-time goodwill credit for the remaining minutes (calculated pro rata) while committing to a joint post-mortem.

Agree with the blended approach. Technical notes below:

- Probe coverage: DataMap ran probes from 7 vantage points; our server-side traces show errors from two of our POPs and a spike in 502/504 at 21:11–21:15. However, the error payloads include upstream TCP resets where our edge was healthy but the next hop returned RSTs. That points to third-party transit degradation around 21:11–21:15.
- Maintenance impact: The config change touched the edge TLS handshake policy which briefly increased handshake latency and triggered retry storms on older TCP stacks; this maps to 21:06–21:10 on our telemetry.
- Conclusion: split causes — 4m attributable to our maintenance (excluded per SLA), 4m attributable to third-party transit (deny), 3m mixed (offer goodwill).

I'm attaching: redwood-traces-20270612.csv (per-POP request/response table), kv-cache-metrics.log (cache hit ratios during window). Use these in the response.

Ben
Senior SRE | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-traces-20270612.csv, kv-cache-metrics.log

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Jacob Lee <jacob.lee@datamap.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2027 16:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Final position on 2027-06-12 partial degradation / next steps

Jacob — thanks for your patience while we investigated. Below is our final determination and next steps.

Summary of findings:
- Maintenance exclusion: We will exclude the scheduled maintenance window 21:00–21:10 UTC (change CH-1927) from SLA calculations as requested. This accounts for 4 minutes of the customer-reported window and is consistent with the SLA section on announced maintenance.
- Residual impact: For 21:11–21:17 UTC (7 minutes), our traces identify a mix of third-party transit resets (AS64532) and a smaller subset caused by elevated TLS handshake latency immediately after the rollout. Per our policy, minutes where the primary root cause is third-party transit are not eligible for SLA credit.
- Offer: To preserve the partnership, Redwood will issue a one-time goodwill credit equal to 25% of the pro-rated SLA credit for the 3 minutes we classify as mixed-cause impact (not the full 7 minutes). We will deny credit for minutes where third-party transit is the primary cause.

Deliverables and timeline:
- Attached: credit-note-DataMap-20270630.pdf (formal credit note and calculation breakdown).
- We propose a joint post-mortem next Wednesday (calendar invite to follow) and will provide the full packet-level traces and traceroutes in the support ticket.
- If you disagree with the attribution, we can open an arbitration-style review with additional telemetry (mutual packet captures) within 7 days.

Please confirm you accept the credit and the proposed post-mortem window and I'll route the credit for processing.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
